zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue directly states that a specific attribute value belongs to a particular house number, assign it right away to reduce the search space.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a fixed house number for an attribute (e.g., "Eric is in the third house").
zebralogic.example: Delaying the placement of a fixed‑position clue and treating it as a later constraint, causing unnecessary branching.

zebralogic.title: Translate direct adjacency into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is directly left/right of Y, enforce that X and Y occupy adjacent houses with the correct orientation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For clues containing "directly left of" or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "X is directly left of Y" as only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y)) without requiring adjacency.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating "N houses between X and Y" means there are exactly N houses separating them, i.e., |pos(X)‑pos(Y)| = N+1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For clues that specify a number of houses between two items.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "There are 2 houses between X and Y" as a distance of 2 instead of the correct distance of 3.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "The milk drinker has a hamster"), treat them as belonging to the same house and propagate both directions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue links two attributes with words like "is", "has", or "the ... who".
zebralogic.example: Treating "The milk drinker has a hamster" as two separate facts instead of binding milk and hamster to the same house.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), not adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For clues containing "somewhere left of" or "somewhere right of".
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "X is somewhere left of Y" as if X must be directly adjacent to Y.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue forbids an attribute from a specific house (e.g., "Peter is not in the fifth house"), eliminate that possibility immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For clues that explicitly state that something is not in a given house.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring "Peter is not in the fifth house" and allowing Peter to be placed there.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; after assigning a value, remove it from the candidate sets of the other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Continuously throughout solving, after any assignment.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same food to two different houses, violating the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final solution, write each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, including case and spelling.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During the final answer construction, before serialising to JSON.
zebralogic.example: Changing "sept" to "september" or altering the case of a name.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a domain for a variable is reduced to a single option.
zebralogic.example: Leaving a house's food undefined even though only one food remains possible, causing unnecessary ambiguity.

zebralogic.title: Validate final answer completeness and JSON structure
zebralogic.principle: Before submitting, ensure the JSON object is syntactically complete, contains all houses, and follows the required schema.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After constructing the solution but before output.
zebralogic.example: Truncating the JSON output so that the closing brackets or some rows are missing.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the number of houses as the absolute distance, forgetting that 'N houses between' implies a gap of N houses, i.e., distance N+1.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says 'N houses between X and Y', enforce |pos(X)‑pos(Y)| = N+1, not N.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model processes each part of the clue independently, missing that they refer to the same house.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue links two attributes (e.g., 'The milk drinker has a hamster'), treat them as a single combined constraint on one house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may assign the same value to multiple houses because it does not enforce global uniqueness across a category.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After any assignment, remove that value from the candidate sets of all other houses in the same category.

zebralogic.description: Truncating the final answer, resulting in incomplete JSON
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model reaches the token limit or stops generation early, leaving the JSON structure unfinished.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Generate the full JSON in one go, double‑check that all opening brackets have matching closing ones, and count rows to ensure all houses are present.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model assumes abbreviations or case changes are equivalent and rewrites values, but the verifier expects the exact strings from the problem.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When writing the solution, copy each attribute value exactly as given in the puzzle, without expanding abbreviations or changing case.
